rows.fact: Existing mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability are reported as of January 2026.
The Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises.
The 24.9 million full-fibre premises represented 82% of 30.5 million UK homes.
Full-fibre availability increased by 1.2 million homes in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up at all premises reached 12.4 million connections.
Full-fibre take-up increased by 1.8 million connections in six months.
Full-fibre take-up equalled 47% of all premises with access to full fibre.
Gigabit-capable availability reached 89% of UK homes.
Gigabit-capable availability covered 27.1 million homes.
Gigabit availability increased from 87% in July 2025 to 89% in January 2026.
Gigabit-covered homes increased from 26.4 million to 27.1 million.
Fixed broadband reporting includes fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access availability.
Decent broadband is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
The update separately discusses affordable Starlink access for some premises without decent fixed or FWA service.
The Spring update is a current-coverage snapshot and not a deployment forecast.
The planned-deployments report was published on 13 May 2026.
The forecast uses operator plans stated as of January 2026.
The report examines planned coverage through the end of 2028.
Full fibre could reach 28.1 million UK homes by the end of 2028.
The 28.1 million forecast corresponds to 92% of residential properties.
Gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29 million homes.
The gigabit-capable forecast corresponds to 95% of homes.
At least two gigabit-capable networks could cover 22.2 million homes.
The two-network forecast corresponds to 73% of homes.
At least three gigabit-capable networks could cover 11.1 million homes.
The three-network forecast corresponds to 36% of homes.
Around 6,950 additional or upgraded FWA masts are planned from January 2026 to January 2029.
High-confidence plans require at least Low Level Design Complete and committed funding.
The report includes privately funded and publicly supported operator plans.
Public-authority aspirations are not separately included unless reflected in operator plans.
Ofcom states that planned-deployment figures are not comprehensive or definitive.
The product cross-references UPRNs, USRNs and TOIDs.
The product is updated every six weeks.
The downloadable relationship table is provided in CSV format.
The product is a look-up table.
UPRN and USRN relationships come from the bodies responsible for those identifier schemes.
Ordnance Survey spatially matches identifiers to OS MasterMap features.
The API is updated every six weeks.
The API conforms to RESTful OpenAPI 3.0.2.
The API returns identifier relationship data in JSON.
The API links property UPRNs to street USRNs and other OS MasterMap identifiers.
OS Open UPRN contains coordinates for UPRNs across Great Britain.
OS Open UPRN is updated every six weeks.
OS Open UPRN is available in CSV and GeoPackage formats.
UPRNs cover approximately 40 million addressable locations.
A TOID is unique and persistent and is never reused.
OS Open TOID is updated every six weeks and is available as CSV and GeoPackage.
INSPIRE Index Polygons show registered freehold property locations in England and Wales.
The dataset is a subset of HM Land Registry's Index Polygons database.
Polygons show the position and indicative extent of registered property.
Files are divided by local authority area.
A boundary-crossing polygon can appear in both local-authority files.
Each polygon has a Land Registry INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
The INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan information.
The July 2026 INSPIRE files were published on 5 July 2026.
New INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
Polygons can be downloaded by local authority.
A GIS is required to view the downloaded polygon data.
Downloads are supplied under Open Government Licence conditions.
The national catalogue entry was last updated on 8 July 2026.
The catalogue describes coverage as England and Wales freehold registered property.
The geometry is indicative and does not by itself establish the project's parcel identifier.
INSPIRE ID is not a UPRN; a trusted project parcel-to-UPRN/geometry bridge is still required.
